title: Two Friends Discuss Ibrahim's Trust Over Coffee
script: Nadia: [curious] Bilal, I've been reading about Prophet Ibrahim lately. His trust in Allah amazes me.
Bilal: Same here. Which part are you thinking about right now?
Nadia: [thoughtful] The part where he was still young, and he broke the idols his own people worshipped.
Bilal: Right, and then he calmly told them to ask the biggest idol what happened, knowing it couldn't speak.
Nadia: [amazed] That takes real courage, standing alone against everyone's beliefs like that.
Bilal: It does. He wasn't afraid to question something everyone around him accepted without thinking.
Nadia: [serious] I also think about later, when Allah tested him by asking him to leave Hajar and baby Ismail in the desert.
Bilal: That part is hard to imagine. Yet Hajar trusted Allah too, asking simply if Allah had commanded it.
Nadia: [softly] When Ibrahim said yes, she said then Allah will not abandon us. That line stays with me.
Bilal: [relieved] And Allah didn't abandon them. The well of Zamzam appeared right there, exactly when they needed water.
Nadia: It still exists today, doesn't it? People drink from it during pilgrimage.
Bilal: Yes, pilgrims still drink Zamzam water today.
Nadia: [reflective] What strikes me most is that Ibrahim kept trusting Allah through every single test, one after another.
Bilal: Trust in Allah may be needed many times and in different tests.
Nadia: That's a good reminder for me honestly. My own trust gets shaky after just one hard week.
Bilal: Mine too, if I'm honest. Maybe that's why we keep returning to his story, again and again.
Nadia: I think that's exactly why these old stories still matter for people living completely different lives today.
Bilal: [warmly] Agreed. Our lives are different, but we still need courage and trust in Allah.

quiz.question: What did the young Ibrahim do to his people's idols?
quiz.explanation: Nadia mentions that Ibrahim, while still young, broke the idols his people worshipped.

quiz.question: What did Ibrahim tell his people to do afterward?
options: Ask the biggest idol what happened
quiz.explanation: Bilal explains Ibrahim calmly told them to ask the biggest idol, knowing it could not speak.

quiz.question: What did Hajar say when Ibrahim told her Allah commanded him to leave her and Ismail?
options: She asked him to stay instead
She said Allah will not abandon us
quiz.explanation: Hajar said that if Allah commanded it, then Allah will not abandon them.

quiz.question: What appeared to help Hajar and Ismail in the desert?
quiz.explanation: The well of Zamzam appeared exactly when Hajar and Ismail needed water.

quiz.question: What do Nadia and Bilal conclude about trust?
options: It is tested only once in life
It gets tested repeatedly throughout a whole life
quiz.explanation: They conclude that true trust isn't tested once, but repeatedly, in different ways, throughout a whole life.

quiz.question: Why did Ibrahim tell the people to ask the largest idol?
options: To learn who made the idols
To show that an idol could not speak
quiz.explanation: The question showed the idol’s lack of power.

quiz.question: Who asked whether Allah had commanded the desert journey?
quiz.explanation: Hajar’s question led to her statement of trust.

quiz.question: What appeared in the desert?
quiz.explanation: Water came when Hajar and Ismail needed it.

quiz.question: What does “shaky” mean when Nadia describes her trust?
quiz.explanation: She says one difficult week can weaken her confidence.

quiz.question: Why do the friends return to Ibrahim’s story?
options: It reminds them to trust Allah in tests
They want to count old idols
They are planning a mountain trip
quiz.explanation: They connect his example with challenges in their own lives.
